plan.title: All About Me
plan.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers will explore who they are through activities focused on their names, families, bodies, feelings, preferences, and unique characteristics. Through books, songs, art, mirrors, movement, and discussions, children will build self-awareness, confidence, communication skills, and positive relationships with others.
plan.objectives:
Develop self-awareness and confidence
Learn and recognize their names and letters in names
Explore body parts and facial features
Build emotional awareness and vocabulary
Strengthen communication skills
Celebrate similarities and differences among peers
plan.weeklyMaterials:
Child photos
Family photos
Mirrors
Name cards
Crayons and markers
Paper and paint
Emotion cards
Building blocks
Scarves for friendship path
Blocks and linking cubes for tower measuring
plan.vocabularyWords:
me
name
family
friend
happy
sad
eyes
nose
hands
body
same
different
special
plan.familyConnection: Invite families to share photos and talk about family members. Encourage children to practice saying their names and identifying body parts at home.
plan.observationOpportunities: Observe self-recognition, emotional awareness, communication skills, social interactions, confidence, and participation.
plan.adaptations: Provide visual supports, family photos, and individualized assistance as needed. Encourage participation at each child's comfort level.

songs.title: If You're Happy and You Know It

monday.theme: All About Me: Mirror Me & Name Discovery
monday.objectives:
Build self-awareness at the mirror.
Recognize preferred names and first letters.
Share people who care for me without ranking families.
monday.materials:
Child-safe mirrors, emotion cards
Name cards, photos, letter magnets
Family photos, photo display board
monday.vocabulary: me, name, family, friend, happy, sad
circleTime: Morning greeting and brief share connected to all about me.
Sing "If You're Happy and You Know It" and preview today's focus: introduce the theme through literacy, sensory, and language play.
Read or revisit I Like Myself! by Karen Beaumont and ask 1–2 open-ended theme questions before centers.
monday.outdoorPlay: Outdoor gross-motor exploration connected to all about me — movement games, collaborative challenges, or nature observation linked to today's indoor activities (Mirror Me / My Name Discovery).
observations: Participation and interest in All About Me play
monday.adaptations: Provide visual supports, family photos, and individualized assistance as needed. Encourage participation at each child's comfort level.
monday.safetyNotes: Supervise active play and tools; review allergy considerations; keep aisles clear during centers and outdoor games.

items.title: Mirror Me
items.objective: Develop self-awareness through observation.
items.description: Preschoolers explore their reflections and identify facial features using mirrors.
items.setup: Place mirrors at child eye level with emotion cards nearby.
items.steps:
1. Invite children to look into mirrors.
2. Point out eyes, nose, mouth, and ears.
3. Encourage children to identify features on themselves.
4. Make faces to match emotion cards.
5. Discuss what makes each face unique.
items.teacherRole: Model vocabulary and encourage observation.
items.observationOpportunities:
Identifies facial features
Engages with reflection
Uses vocabulary
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: My Name Discovery
items.objective: Recognize and become familiar with individual names.
items.description: Preschoolers explore name cards and practice identifying their own names.
items.setup: Arrange name cards on a table with photos.
items.steps:
1. Show each child's name card and say the name aloud.
2. Match photos to names.
3. Encourage children to find their own card.
4. Clap syllables in each name.
5. Celebrate when children locate their name.
items.teacherRole: Help children recognize their names and connect names with photos.
items.observationOpportunities:
Recognizes own name
Matches photo correctly
Participates willingly
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: Family Photo Sharing
items.objective: Strengthen family connections and communication.
items.description: Preschoolers explore family photos and talk about important people in their lives.
items.setup: Display photos at child level on a board.
items.steps:
1. Show family photos submitted by families.
2. Name family members in each photo.
3. Encourage children to point and identify.
4. Talk about how families are similar and different.
5. Celebrate each child's family.
items.teacherRole: Encourage discussion and model language.
items.observationOpportunities:
Identifies family members
Communicates about family
Engages in discussion
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: Body Part Movement Game
items.objective: Identify body parts through active play.
items.description: Preschoolers touch named body parts during a movement song and game.
items.materials: Open space, body part picture cards
items.setup: Clear space for movement with picture cards visible.
items.steps:
1. Review body part names with picture cards.
2. Play Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes.
3. Call out parts for children to touch.
4. Add silly parts like elbows and ankles.
5. Cool down with deep breaths.
items.teacherRole: Call body parts and model movements.
items.observationOpportunities:
Touches correct body part
Follows movement song
Uses body vocabulary
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.

items.title: Self-Portrait Studio

items.title: Celebration Circle
items.objective: Celebrate unique qualities of each child.
items.description: Preschoolers share something special about themselves during a closing celebration circle.
items.setup: Gather in circle with name cards visible.
items.steps:
1. Invite each child to share one special thing about themselves.
2. Classmates listen and clap after each share.
3. Sing The More We Get Together.
4. Give celebration stickers.
5. Review how the class learned about each friend.
items.teacherRole: Facilitate positive sharing and group appreciation.
items.observationOpportunities:
Shares about self
Listens to peers
Participates in celebration

items.title: All About Me Movement Parade
items.objective: Express identity through movement and music.
items.description: Preschoolers parade with scarves or instruments showing favorite movements.
items.setup: Line up parade path in open space.
items.steps:
1. Each child chooses a movement that feels like them.
2. Parade around the room to music.
3. Stop to show movement when music pauses.
4. Cheer for each friend's movement.
5. End with a group hug or high-five line.

items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: All About Me Book Making
items.objective: Create a simple book about personal favorites.
items.description: Preschoolers dictate or draw pages about their favorites for a class book.
items.setup: Prepare book pages with prompts like My favorite food.
items.steps:
1. Complete pages about favorites (food, toy, color).
2. Add drawings or photos to each page.
3. Assemble pages into a book.
4. Read the finished book together.
5. Place book in library center.
items.teacherRole: Write children's dictation and read pages aloud.
items.observationOpportunities:
Contributes a page
Dictates or draws ideas
Listens to compiled book
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: Body Outline Tracing
items.objective: Explore body shape and spatial awareness.
items.description: Preschoolers trace a partner's body outline on large paper and add details.
items.setup: Tape large paper to the floor in open area.
items.steps:
1. One child lies still while a partner traces around them.
2. Switch roles so each child has an outline.
3. Add facial features and clothing.
4. Label body parts together.
5. Display outlines in the hallway.
items.teacherRole: Supervise tracing and encourage labeling body parts.
items.observationOpportunities:
Cooperates during tracing
Labels body parts
Works with a partner
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: Celebration Circle
items.objective: Celebrate unique qualities of each child.
items.description: Preschoolers share something special about themselves during a closing celebration circle.
items.setup: Gather in circle with name cards visible.
items.steps:
1. Invite each child to share one special thing about themselves.
2. Classmates listen and clap after each share.
3. Sing The More We Get Together.
4. Give celebration stickers.
5. Review how the class learned about each friend.
items.teacherRole: Facilitate positive sharing and group appreciation.
items.observationOpportunities:
Shares about self
Listens to peers
Participates in celebration
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

items.title: All About Me Movement Parade
items.objective: Express identity through movement and music.
items.description: Preschoolers parade with scarves or instruments showing favorite movements.
items.setup: Line up parade path in open space.
items.steps:
1. Each child chooses a movement that feels like them.
2. Parade around the room to music.
3. Stop to show movement when music pauses.
4. Cheer for each friend's movement.
5. End with a group hug or high-five line.
items.teacherRole: Lead parade and invite creative movement.
items.observationOpportunities:
Chooses personal movement
Participates in parade
Shows confidence
items.adaptations: Provide visual steps, partner support, or a simplified materials set. Extend with an open-ended challenge for children ready for more.
items.safetyNotes: Supervise tools and materials, review allergy-safe consumables, and keep pathways clear during active or outdoor play.

week.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers study identity through mirrors, names, chosen families, feelings art, and cooperative movement. We avoid body comparisons and celebrate many ways to look, move, and belong.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Child-safe mirrors
Name cards and chunky letters
Family photos or drawings
Skin-tone crayons
Paper and clipboards
Blocks and cubes
Scarves and ribbon
Picture card pack PDF
Stickers or paper dots
Stapler (adult)
Play kitchen props
Emotion/interest cards
week.teacherPreparation: Print All About Me Picture Card Pack. Request optional family photos with privacy note. Set skin-tone crayons out. Replace any height charts that rank children.
week.familyConnection: Invite families to send a drawing or photo of people/pets who care for the child, or to share a preferred name pronunciation audio.
milestones: Language: Uses name and feeling words
SEL: Shows interest in peers’ preferences
Cognition: Matches letters in own name
Motor: Draws process portraits and builds towers
Creativity: Dictates pages for a personal book

songs.title: I Am Me (LLH Affirmation)
songs.rightsEvidence: Original LLH affirmation chant written for All About Me preschool week.
songs.lyrics:
I am me, you are you,
Different hair and feelings too.
Clap for you and clap for me,
We belong here—1, 2, 3!
songs.motions: Point to self; point to friend; touch hair; heart hands; clap three times.
songs.teacherDirections: Teach seated first. Invite whispered verse for shy voices.
songs.whenToUse: Monday mirror time and Friday celebration.

songs.title: Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes
songs.rightsEvidence: Traditional children's movement song; longstanding oral tradition in English-language early childhood, treated as public domain in standard ECE practice. Provide seated/adapted motions for all bodies.
songs.lyrics:
Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes.
Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes.
And eyes and ears and mouth and nose,
Head, shoulders, knees and toes, knees and toes.
songs.motions: Touch each named part; offer alternatives (elbows, wheels, tips of shoes).
songs.teacherDirections: Model inclusive substitutions aloud so every body is included.
songs.suggestedPace: Start slow; speed only if children request.
songs.transitionPurpose: Warm up body awareness without comparison.

songs.title: The More We Get Together
songs.rightsEvidence: Traditional folk song derived from older European folk melodies; widely used as public-domain children's repertoire in ECE. Lyrics are the traditional English children's verse.
songs.lyrics:
The more we get together, together, together,
The more we get together, the happier we'll be.
For your friends are my friends, and my friends are your friends,
The more we get together, the happier we'll be.
songs.motions: Sway side to side; point to friends; gather hands only with consent.
songs.teacherDirections: Use at celebration circle; offer solitary sway option.
songs.transitionPurpose: Close the week with community language.
